post.caption: He thought it was a powder compact. In September 1985, a metal detectorist found it near Middleham Castle. It is gold, set with a blue sapphire of about 10 carats, and he had forgotten to turn off his detector while walking back to his car. On the back, the Nativity sits above the Lamb of God, and the pendant dates from the late 1400s. The back slides open to a hidden space, probably for a relic, and people believed its sapphire could cure ulcers. In 1992 the Yorkshire Museum bought it for 2.5 million pounds, after a public appeal. The original is displayed in York.
